text:
Morgan Frost is doing in Calgary what he never quite got to do in Philadelphia: play real minutes in the middle without anyone wondering if he belongs. He has five goals and 13 points in 22 games, six of them on the power play, and his scoring rate (2.34 points per 60) sits just above the top of what we'd expect from his talent range. His goal against the Kings last week broke a 1-1 tie on the road.

The caution is in the quieter numbers. Over his last 10 his own chances have dried up, 0.7 expected goals against the 2.1 we'd expect, and Calgary holds 45.8% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. That last part needs context: Evolving-Hockey had him playing with some of the weakest teammates in the league last season and still worth 1.7 wins, 73rd among 401 forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking describes his game: 61% of his entries are carries, and 61% of his shots come off the rush. When the Flames get the puck back, watch where he goes.
